title: Iran Proposes Seven-Day Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz, End War
detail: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, after Qatar-mediated talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the UN, presented a plan built on the defunct June 17 memorandum of understanding: a seven-day cessation of hostilities across the region (including Lebanon), release of at least $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets, lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the US naval blockade, with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz on day seven of the truce. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it would be wrong to call the talks a breakthrough, and the administration has not committed to reviving the June MoU's terms.

media.caption: Iran's foreign minister proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war

title: NCRI: 78 Executions Documented in One Month, Including 6 Women, 9 Baluch Citizens
detail: The National Council of Resistance of Iran documented 78 executions across 24 prisons between Aug 23 and Sep 22, 2026 (the Iranian month of Shahrivar 1405), including 6 women and 9 Baluch citizens — the heaviest tolls at Isfahan's Dastgerd Prison (15) and Mashhad's Vakilabad Prison (10). Named cases include Mostafa Karimzadeh (Isfahan, Sep 22) and Eskandar Heydarzadeh (Tabriz, Sep 14). NCRI said the true toll is likely higher, echoing Human Rights Watch's Sep 10 finding that at least 59 men were arbitrarily executed on national-security charges over five months following unfair trials, several of them teenagers, five hanged publicly.
